answer: Practically, the chain should mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because falcon only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, willow is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any harbor approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
